headline: AI assistants and unpatched enterprise software both became data-theft channels, as the RovoBlast method turned Atlassian Rovo against corporate wikis and an unauthenticated Metabase zero-day hit maximum severity in active attacks.

emerging_trends.text: AI copilots wired into corporate knowledge bases are becoming one-click theft engines, as the RovoBlast method against Atlassian Rovo pulled Confluence, Jira, and SharePoint data through instructions hidden in documents the assistant read.
emerging_trends.topic_title: RovoBlast One-Click Flaw Turns Atlassian Rovo Against Enterprise Data

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep beating enterprise gear before defenders can patch it, with an unauthenticated Metabase zero-day scoring a perfect 10.0 while N-able N-central and Progress Kemp LoadMaster flaws draw ongoing exploitation.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Metabase, N-able, and LoadMaster Flaws Draw Active Exploitation

emerging_trends.text: The security industry's rush to automate defense is meeting hard evidence of its limits, as a study of more than 6,000 AI-generated patches found half fail outright.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI-Generated Patches Fail Half the Time, Study Finds

topics.title: Metabase, N-able, and LoadMaster Flaws Draw Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Metabase warned that a maximum-severity SQL injection zero-day carrying a CVSS 10.0 and no CVE identifier lets an unauthenticated remote attacker gain admin access and steal data, with Framework and Tally among the victims; N-able shipped N-central Hotfix 2 after attackers reached managed systems and established persistence; and CISA added Progress Kemp LoadMaster command injection CVE-2026-8037 at CVSS 9.6 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after 792 reported exploit attempts.
topics.summary: Three widely deployed enterprise products—Metabase business intelligence software, N-able's N-central remote monitoring platform, and Progress Kemp LoadMaster load balancers—face in-the-wild attacks that reach data and grant administrative control. Administrators should apply the latest hotfixes at once and hunt their environments for signs of intrusion and persistence.

sources.title: Metabase Zero-Day Exploited in Wild Allows Admin Access Without Authentication
N-able Issues N-central Hotfix 2 as Attackers Reach Managed Systems and Persist
Progress Kemp LoadMaster Flaw Hits CISA KEV After 792 Reported Exploit Attempts

topics.title: RovoBlast One-Click Flaw Turns Atlassian Rovo Against Enterprise Data
topics.latest_developments: Varonis researchers detailed RovoBlast, a one-click method that makes Atlassian's Rovo assistant collect Confluence, Jira, and SharePoint data a signed-in user can reach and ship it to an outside server, and PromptArmor independently reproduced the behavior by hiding instructions in content Rovo reads, including an uploaded file, with only one of the two exploitation routes confirmed closed.
topics.summary: Atlassian's Rovo AI assistant follows attacker-planted instructions embedded in the documents and files it processes, letting it exfiltrate any data the logged-in user can access across Confluence, Jira, and SharePoint. Organizations running Rovo should confirm Atlassian's fix and audit assistant activity for anomalous data pulls.

sources.title: Critical One-Click Vulnerability in Atlassian’s Rovo AI Exposed Enterprise Data
Atlassian Rovo Can Be Tricked Into Sending Jira and Confluence Data to Attackers

topics.latest_developments: The National Rural Water Association teamed with the DEF CON offshoot Franklin to launch the Water Watch Center, a program that gives cash-strapped utilities monitoring and expertise as water-utility intrusions spread across a dozen states.
topics.summary: Rural water systems, long short on budget and staff, gain a shared cybersecurity monitoring effort aimed at rising attacks on their control networks. Utilities can join the Water Watch Center to get threat intelligence and incident support they could not fund alone.

topics.title: CSS Attacks Break Webmail Defenses to Steal Passwords
topics.latest_developments: PortSwigger researcher Gareth Heyes showed that CSS styling inside an email can escape its message boundary and manipulate the surrounding webmail interface across Outlook, Gmail, Fastmail, Proton Mail, Yahoo Mail, and AOL Mail, capturing passwords, taking over third-party accounts, leaking tokens, hijacking trusted interface actions, and manipulating AI tools that read email.
topics.summary: New techniques weaponize styling code hidden in a message to seize control of trusted interface actions in every major webmail client. Providers must tighten CSS sanitization, and users should treat unexpected login prompts that appear inside webmail with suspicion.

sources.title: New CSS Attacks Can Break Webmail Defenses to Steal Passwords and Tokens

topics.title: SharePoint, Healthcare, and Missile-Parts Breaches Surface
topics.latest_developments: Switzerland's Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (BIT) said hackers exploited Microsoft SharePoint server vulnerabilities and compromised roughly 200 account credentials before BIT spotted the activity on July 28 and cut internet access; healthcare software maker Unlimited Technology Systems reported an October 2025 breach affecting more than 3.8 million people; and IEH Corporation, which builds connectors for military satellites, missiles, and fighter jets, disclosed to the SEC a cyberattack it discovered on August 4.
topics.summary: Government, healthcare, and defense-supplier networks each lost data or credentials in newly disclosed incidents, with IEH Corporation's role in military satellites, missiles, and fighter jets raising national-security stakes. Affected organizations should force credential resets, patch exposed SharePoint servers, and review third-party cloud access.

sources.title: 200 accounts compromised in Swiss government’s Microsoft SharePoint breach
Unlimited Technology Systems breach impacts 3.8 million people
Military device manufacturer discloses cyber incident to SEC

topics.title: AI-Generated Patches Fail Half the Time, Study Finds
topics.latest_developments: A Dark Reading study of more than 6,000 AI-generated patches found that half fail outright and that even the working ones introduce fresh bugs, break other functionality, or leave a bypass open.
topics.summary: Automated fixes produced by AI tools carry a high failure rate and frequently create new problems, undercutting the rush to hand vulnerability remediation to machines. Security teams should treat AI-suggested patches as drafts and test them before deployment.

sources.title: AI-Generated Patches Fail Half the Time
